summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen on Wednesday to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting ahead of a historic three-way summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

According to the White House schedule, Trump is set to hold a bilateral meeting with Xi at Kylin Villa on Thursday afternoon before joining Xi and Putin for the first face-to-face trilateral gathering among the three heads of state in history.

Trump has stated that he plans to press Moscow and Beijing on a modernized three-way nuclear arms control framework—including potential limits on artificial intelligence in nuclear command systems—alongside negotiations over the war in Ukraine and diplomatic pressure on Iran.

Ahead of Trump's arrival, Putin and Xi met bilaterally in Shenzhen on Wednesday morning, where the Russian leader asserted that Western sanctions over Ukraine had backfired while European allies watched warily for signs of a great-power bargain affecting regional security.

summary: On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Democrat Mary Peltola unseated two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, flipping Alaska's Senate seat to Democratic control for the first time in 18 years and marking the ninth seat Democrats flipped this midterm.

Allegations that Peltola's campaign recruited retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan as a spoiler candidate roiled the race, prompting Trump to order the Justice Department to sue to block certification if the incumbent lost.

Peltola secured 50% of first-choice votes, rendering ranked-choice tabulation unnecessary; a federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit on Nov. 1, ruling such action would "clearly violate" voters' ballot secrecy rights.

With 56 seats, Democrats hold their largest Senate majority in 16 years when the new Congress convenes, surpassing the 53-47 margin Republicans held before the midterms and completing a nine-seat wave.

Peltola will become the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. Senate , sharing this historic milestone with Minnesota Democratic Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan, marking a breakthrough for Indigenous representation in Congress.
title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins US Senate race in Alaska, beating incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan

summary: On Tuesday, the Federal Aviation Administration paused installation of new routers following a nationwide ground stop last Friday, also disabling existing Juniper routers after a device in El Dorado, Arkansas, overloaded communications systems.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the system overload stemmed from a new router installed by contractor L3Harris Technologies, which triggered "excessive data" that flooded network feeds at 17 of 22 regional air traffic control centers.

For now, the FAA is relying on 25-year-old Cisco routers to maintain operations while investigating the failure; the Senate Commerce Committee reported L3Harris installed 400 of 3,648 planned routers, with only 69 currently operational.

Democratic senators demanded the Trump administration explain the failure, writing that "identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed," while the agency invited the FBI to assist in reviewing hardware at an L3Harris lab in Florida.

The Trump administration updated its request to Congress for $50.1 billion to improve airports and traffic control systems, following last year's $12.5 billion approval to modernize infrastructure relied upon by more than 45,000 daily flights.
title: FAA halts installation of routers that led to ground stop

Jeffries campaigned across the country in recent months, helping Democrats win a projected 259 seats—the largest majority in 35 years—providing substantial cushion for the January 3, 2027, floor vote where he needs 218 votes.

Rep. Shomari Figures of Alabama endorsed Jeffries, saying he "led us through what is likely the most tumultuous two-year tenure of any presidency in the history of this nation." Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez confirmed Jeffries is "listening to ideas" from progressives.

summary: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, according to detailed projections released Wednesday by the Pew Research Center. Both faiths are growing, but Islam is expanding much faster.

Higher fertility rates drive this demographic shift, with Muslim women averaging 3.1 children compared to 2.5 for Christians. Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett emphasized that fertility, not conversion, is the primary factor.

By 2035, Pew forecasts 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians worldwide. If recent trends continue, those figures will reach more than 3.6 billion and just under 3 billion, respectively, by 2070.

Gina Zurlo, a senior researcher at Harvard Divinity School, warned that "many Christians are not happy" about these trends, causing "angst." She urged greater interreligious education to "humanize" the "other" and reduce misunderstanding.

Beyond the two major faiths, the population of people who are atheist, agnostic, or religiously unaffiliated will grow by more than 180 million by 2070. South Korea, France, and the United Kingdom are forecast to join this demographic group.
title: Pew Projects Islam Will Surpass Christianity by 2035

summary: The Air Force launched an unarmed Minuteman III ICBM from Vandenberg Space Force Base late Tuesday, coinciding with the APEC summit in Shenzhen where President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping , and Russian President Vladimir Putin plan to discuss nuclear arms control.
Designated Glory Trip 257, the launch was planned five years ago by Air Force Global Strike Command and is not a response to current diplomatic events, the command said.

Minuteman III missiles serve as the land-based component of the United States nuclear triad, with about 400 currently on alert across Montana, North Dakota, and Wyoming. These systems have operated for over five decades, far exceeding their original ten-year expected service life.

According to Air Force General S.L. Davis, such tests are "foundational to ensuring the safety and surety of the Minuteman system." The launch occurred as the White House reported world leaders will discuss potential nuclear weapons limits.

The Air Force plans to replace the aging Minuteman III fleet with the LGM-35A Sentinel, though the program has faced delays and ballooning costs. Older missiles are expected to remain in service for years as modernization continues.

Harding decided to keep the SUV, saying, 'The three of us feel very connected to it.' Tracking site FlightAware reported about 18,000 flight cancellations as of Monday from the ground stop.

summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, sending players back to Vice City after a 13-year wait since the franchise's predecessor. The game is set in Leonida, Rockstar Games' sprawling fictional version of Florida.

At the center of the game are protagonists Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple whose attempts to improve their lives pull them deeper into the criminal underworld. Their story unfolds in a "Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story" after an easy score goes wrong.

With eight nominations for the Game Awards, including game of the year, GTA VI has attracted significant recognition before release. Its 212 gigabyte file size is expected to drive about 35 petabytes of additional network traffic globally.

Miami-Dade County entered a $3.9 million promotional deal with Rockstar featuring a "Welcome to Vice City" display atop the Kaseya Center. Some officials have questioned using public resources to promote a franchise known for criminal activity.

Gamers are discussing online how to trick their consoles into thinking they are based in New Zealand to unlock the game earlier. This frenzy reflects massive anticipation for one of 2026's biggest gaming launches.
title: After a 13-year wait, ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ arrives with enormous hype and expectations

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the story as an ethics and accountability issue, emphasizing Lutnick’s family ties, a “huge financial interest,” and an Nvidia “scandal,” while right-leaning coverage shifts toward national security, chip smuggling, and China, warning that “pulling on a thread” could “unravel much more.” Center coverage bridges both, foregrounding whether Lutnick helped Cantor Fitzgerald avoid losses and whether approving chips for Megaspeed warranted scrutiny.
The dividing line is conflict-of-interest oversight versus export enforcement and geopolitical risk.

Despite contrasting tones—suspicious and accusatory versus ominous and expansive—all perspectives emphasize congressional investigation, Nvidia-linked interests, and potential consequences for U.S. technology policy.
summary: On Wednesday, Democratic lawmakers launched a probe into whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick used his office to assist Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm now run by his sons, avoid losses linked to Nvidia 's scandal.

Investigators are scrutinizing why Lutnick allegedly resisted implementing export controls on Megaspeed and other companies suspected of funneling advanced AI chips to China, potentially compromising national security interests.

Cantor Fitzgerald held Nvidia stock valued around $1.2 billion at Lutnick's confirmation, though filings show the firm reported a nearly 50% decline in those holdings between September 2025 and March 2026.
House Democrats Jamie Raskin, Gregory Meeks, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove demanded the firm preserve all documents, calling the allegations "inaccurate" and "baseless" in a statement to CNBC.
The probe adds to mounting pressure on Nvidia as former executive Jensen Huang prepares for December testimony before GOP-led House panels and Sen. Tim Scott has summoned both Huang and Lutnick.
title: Democrats probe whether Howard Lutnick helped Cantor avoid Nvidia losses, FT reports

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the Florida defamation case as a test of accountability, saying the judge “corners Trump” while his “excuses run dry” and portraying presidential status as an attempted escape from questioning.
Center coverage stresses a procedural compromise: Trump gets more time, but a mandatory deposition remains, with the $10 billion stakes and January 22 deadline foregrounded.
Right-Leaning coverage de-emphasizes political confrontation, presenting the matter as procedure surrounding Trump’s allegation that the BBC edited his January 6 speech.

All emphasize the Florida lawsuit and required testimony, but their divergent tones—adversarial, procedural, and allegation-focused—reflect broader disputes over accountability, media conduct, and presidential authority.
summary: On Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz ordered President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by January 22 in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC.
Trump sued the BBC over its editing of his January 6, 2021, speech, alleging the network maliciously spliced clips to suggest he directed the Capitol attack following his election loss to Joe Biden.

The ruling grants a joint request from both sides, providing Trump six more weeks before questioning. Kuntz noted the president is a "willing participant in the proceedings" because he initiated the litigation.
The BBC accepted Trump's offer to be deposed between January 11 and January 22, despite previously accusing him of delays. Kuntz had rejected the network's motion to dismiss on November 10.
Both sides must complete discovery by January 29 and be trial-ready by May 3. Trump's lawyers maintain that his official duties and security needs pose unique scheduling challenges.
title: US judge extends deadline for Trump deposition in BBC defamation case

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the Kuwait strike as institutional negligence, using “tactical failure,” “brushed off warnings,” and “deadly” to foreground accountability and contrast Ramsbottom’s assessment with Hegseth’s description of a “fortified” site.

Center coverage similarly stresses “ignored warnings” and a “deadly miscalculation,” but pivots to allegedly rejected Ukrainian interceptor-drone technology, presenting a specific preventable alternative.

Right-Leaning coverage narrows the issue to the Army’s failure to provide “adequate protection,” while emphasizing the whistleblower complaint, Ramsbottom’s affiliation, and the facility’s proximity—about 65 miles—to Iran.
All highlight six deaths, alleged defensive shortcomings, and national-security stakes, reflecting broader divides over institutional trust, military competence, and Iran’s threat.
summary: On Friday, Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom filed a whistleblower complaint alleging the Army ignored warnings about inadequate defenses at Port Shuaiba, Kuwait, where an Iranian drone strike killed six U.S. soldiers on March 1, 2026.
Ramsbottom alleged the command post lacked dedicated anti-drone protection, a physician, and a fixed aid station, with only one ambulance available during the attack.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth previously insisted troops were "well-protected," describing the drone as a "squirter" that slipped through defenses at a facility he claimed was "fortified."

Sen. Richard Blumenthal demanded Hegseth provide "All force protection assessments" and appear at a classified briefing, stating "The families of the six fallen servicemembers, the wounded survivors, and the American people deserve transparency and accountability."

Democrats have signaled they will probe the administration's handling of the war with Iran next year, as senior officers reported warnings about Iranian Shaheds were repeatedly ignored by Pentagon leadership.
title: Army soldier files whistleblower complaint against the Pentagon over Iranian strike that killed 6 US service members

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds the human and political costs of “painful budget decisions,” portraying Seattle ’s “recurring budget crisis” as an unresolved mismatch between enrollment and school capacity; center coverage widens the lens, invoking a “stark warning,” “fierce neighborhood outcry,” nearly a dozen possible closures, a national enrollment trend, and a Stanford study whose findings are not provided.
Right-Leaning coverage largely de-emphasizes distinct ideological interpretation, offering no clear policy assertion beyond fiscal pressure and resistance to closures.

Across perspectives, declining enrollment, auditor recommendations, recurring budget strain, and community resistance—including the 2024 reversal—remain shared ground, exposing tensions between fiscal discipline and protecting local institutions.
summary: Public school enrollment has plummeted by more than 1.4 million students since the pandemic, leaving districts nationwide struggling to downsize and confront painful structural deficits. Federal pandemic relief funds have been exhausted.

Nearly four decades ago, Seattle Public Schools auditors urged closing campuses to avert budget crises, but neighborhood outcry halted the recommendations. History repeated in 2024 when the district scrapped plans to shutter up to a fifth of schools.

San Francisco faces similar pressures, with enrollment falling 10% since 2019 and a $100 million-plus deficit prompting a late 2024 closure proposal. A new $183 million contract with United Educators of San Francisco was reached, though a $26 million deficit remains projected.

Employee pay and benefits account for roughly 80% of district budgets, making school closures yield only modest relief. State takeovers of districts have risen to at least 21 since 2023, according to Chalkbeat, limiting local flexibility.

Despite empty desks nationwide, teacher headcounts have grown by 1% since the pandemic. Stanford researcher Thomas Dee said districts have been "playing Hamlet" on downsizing, while structural deficits persist and students risk academic setbacks.
title: U.S. School Districts Face Enrollment Declines and Budget Deficits

summary: The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, aiming to discourage reliance on the technology without imposing new restrictions that could anger industry or Beijing.

Chinese-Made open-weight models are gaining ground with American companies because they are cheaper than proprietary tools from labs like OpenAI, while officials worry Beijing is using these models to make US firms dependent.

Representatives Andrew Garbarino of New York and John Moolenaar of Michigan launched an investigation into American companies' use of Chinese AI this year, sending letters to Airbnb and Anysphere; US government websites have deployed Alibaba models despite FBI warnings.
Officials are looking at ways to discourage use of Chinese AI through a "name and shame" campaign while maintaining a broader anti-regulation stance on AI development.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in July the administration could sanction Chinese AI companies for intellectual property theft, echoing OSTP director Michael Kratsios's April accusation that China stole US artificial intelligence labs' intellectual property on an "industrial scale.
title: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds prosecutors casting Huawei as a “villain,” while noting the defense’s disagreement; right-leaning coverage narrows attention to allegations that leaders “lied” and “broke the law,” without reporting Huawei’s response.

The center accounts supply more legal context—12 remaining counts, trade-secret theft, alleged Iranian surveillance, employee bonuses, and claims of “crime after crime”—alongside the defense’s “false narrative” argument.

These word choices shift the emotional focus from courtroom characterization to dishonesty and lawbreaking, while the shared emphasis is a nearly concluded U.S. criminal trial involving serious allegations, reflecting contrasting priorities in portraying corporate misconduct and accountability.
summary: On Monday, U.S. prosecutors concluded closing arguments in the criminal trial of Huawei Technologies in New York, alleging the firm used widespread "theft, lies cover-ups" to build its global empire.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Meredith Arfa argued Huawei spent 20 years encouraging a workforce of over 200,000 across 170 countries to steal trade secrets, alleging the company provided equipment to Iran for surveillance.

Defense attorney Brian Heberlig countered that prosecutors "decided Huawei was a criminal enterprise" and built a case from that premise, claiming the government focused on isolated incidents rather than proving conspiracy.
The jury is expected to begin deliberations Wednesday following the two-month-long trial, weighing 12 remaining criminal counts including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud.

Chinese officials condemned the U.S. for "economic bullying" and using national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies, while Huawei has expanded into chipmaking amid broader geopolitical tensions.
title: US prosecutors make final case against Huawei in theft, fraud trial

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the DEFIANCE Act as a morally urgent, bipartisan defense of women and girls, using language like “fight,” “push,” and “no more worthy cause,” while elevating Hilton and AOC as advocates against continuing abuse.

Right-Leaning coverage stresses “justice,” survivors’ “right to sue,” Hilton’s personal exploitation history, and the “unlikely allies” of AOC and Republican Laurel Lee, sometimes adding skepticism through “hopeful” and emphasizing the bill’s stalled House status.
Center coverage de-emphasizes partisan drama, foregrounding Senate passage and procedural delay.

All perspectives highlight nonconsensual sexual deepfakes , victims, bipartisan cooperation, and congressional action, but their framing reflects wider divides over moral urgency, individual legal remedies, and political alliance.
summary: On Tuesday, Paris Hilton returned to Capitol Hill to renew pressure on House lawmakers to pass the stalled DEFIANCE Act, joined by Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Republican Rep. Laurel Lee.
"For 10 months, this critical legislation has sat untouched," Rep. Ocasio-Cortez said, noting the bill passed the Senate unanimously twice during 2024 and earlier this year.
New findings reveal that 50 million people have been victimized by explicit deepfakes, including 83 of the 156 women currently serving in the 119th Congress, Hilton reported.
Appealing to House leadership, Hilton issued a direct plea to House Speaker Mike Johnson, Majority Leader Steve Scalise, and House Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan for a floor vote.

The bill builds on the Take It Down Act, championed by former first lady Melania Trump, while advocates remain "very optimistic" about President Trump and the White House's openness to the legislation.
title: Paris Hilton and victims of sexually explicit deepfakes push for House to pass bill

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the central-Gaza operation as Israeli “aggression,” an “assault” on residential areas and a ceasefire violation, foregrounding “martyrs,” civilian casualties, and families fleeing.

Right-Leaning accounts emphasize an “operation” against Hamas infrastructure in Hamas-controlled territory, highlighting military objectives and a reported fighter hit while de-emphasizing civilian harm; even “offensive” signals battlefield momentum.
Center coverage moderates these poles through “incursion,” geography, evacuation warnings, and casualty distinctions.
The pivotal divide is whether crossing the Yellow Line represents unlawful occupation or security action.

All perspectives acknowledge Israeli movement, Palestinian deaths, Hamas-related targeting, and ceasefire context, reflecting broader disputes over sovereignty, proportionality, and civilian protection.
summary: On Nov 18, Israeli tanks advanced in the central Gaza Strip, with witnesses reporting movement onto the Salahudeen road west of the Yellow Line targeting "Hamas infrastructure."

Israel says Hamas has recently been regrouping and rearming, prompting stepped-up attacks despite an Oct 2025 ceasefire that halted major fighting but failed to secure the Islamist group's disarmament.
Separate Israeli air strikes killed two people in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City earlier on Nov 18, while an air strike near the army raid killed another, Palestinian medics said.

Hamas has accused Israel of attempting to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreement; Gaza health authorities report at least 1,600 Palestinians killed since the ceasefire while the Israeli military reports 5 Israeli soldiers killed.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in the military campaign Israel launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on Oct 7, 2023.
title: Israeli military begins a new thrust in Gaza, witnesses say

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the incident as a Palestinian “response” to “settler attacks,” emphasizing “defend their land” and warnings of “displacement” and property seizure; right-leaning coverage portrays an “attempted terrorist attack ,” labels perpetrators “terrorists,” highlights Israelis’ defensive gunfire, troop deployment, roadblocks, and possible casualties.

The pivotal divide is whether the same violence signifies resistance to settlement pressure or an assault on Israeli security, with “terror” and “attack” intensifying the right’s threat-focused tone while the left foregrounds grievance and legitimacy.
Center coverage, where present, de-emphasizes these interpretations, stressing a “reported attempted attack” under investigation.
All perspectives recognize an unsettled Israeli-Palestinian confrontation involving Israelis and Palestinians, reflecting wider geopolitical and territorial divides.
summary: Overnight from Monday into Tuesday, two Israeli civilians were injured near Jericho in a vehicle-ramming attack and assault. The IDF Spokesperson confirmed terrorists rammed their vehicle into an Israeli car and attacked the occupants with weapons.

The attack occurred in a sensitive friction zone near Jericho, where Jewish families moved into houses in the village of Ein Duyuk al-Tahta earlier this month. This area is under the jurisdiction of the Binyamin Regional Council and adjacent to the Hasmonean Palaces.

While the two Israeli civilians were lightly wounded, Palestinian reports indicate a woman was shot dead during the incident. Forces dispatched to the scene have set up roadblocks, and the IDF is investigating the circumstances.

Yisrael Gantz, head of the Binyamin Regional Council, condemned the incident, stating, "Terrorists tried to murder Israelis tonight." He praised the security Forces for their swift action and reiterated support for settlement efforts.

Gantz has characterized these settlement activities as an effort to reverse the Oslo Accords, which handed Jericho to the Palestinian Authority. Organizers seek to change the reality established by political agreements in recent decades through their continued presence.
title: Israeli Military Says It Is Investigating Reported Attempted Attack in Jericho

bias: Coverage splits over what Huang’s Senate appearance means: the left-identified item uses neutral, procedural language—“testify” in an open hearing—and de-emphasizes committee, China, and political context.

Center reports add Tim Scott’s Banking Committee, intensified scrutiny, Huang’s earlier refusal of Senator Warren’s invitation, and possible House testimony, while describing “ramped up scrutiny” and national-security concerns.

Right-Oriented coverage sharpens the stakes with allegations of Chinese influence, advanced-chip access, and possible misconduct, using charged phrases such as “disgraced” and “China Trail,” though these remain allegations rather than established findings.
All agree Huang will appear; the divide reflects routine oversight versus scandal and geopolitical risk.
summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, marking his first public testimony before Congress.

Huang resigned last Thursday following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, amid reports that the relationship compromised sensitive semiconductor technology to China.

Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones confirmed the board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and rejected his return, as Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress serves as interim head during the successor search.
Despite public support from President Trump and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, the board maintains its decision to separate from Huang after he admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife of 41 years.
Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott seeks to determine if proprietary AI chips were compromised, while House committees conduct a separate investigation into the matter.
title: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says

bias: Left-Leaning coverage emphasizes that Canada’s growing commodity trade with China is “not a top concern” for Trump, contrasting relatively manageable Beijing ties with “much more complex” Canada-U.S. “trade war negotiations.” Right-leaning framing pivots to a customs “dispute,” tariffs, and Carney “defends” trade with Beijing, implying justification is necessary, while a positive “good talk” softens the confrontation.
Center coverage adds logistical and institutional detail—Shenzhen, APEC , a roughly 20-minute meeting, and participating officials—without intensifying either narrative.

All perspectives acknowledge Carney’s claim, the commodity-versus-semiconductor distinction, and the meeting, reflecting shared interest in trade while diverging over China’s strategic meaning and U.S. tariff pressure.
summary: On Nov 18, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said at the APEC summit in Shenzhen that Canada's trade with China is not a top priority for President Donald Trump , noting Canada primarily exports commodities rather than sensitive technologies.

Peter Navarro criticized Carney after the Canadian leader suggested Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with Washington fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.

On Tuesday, Carney met with Chinese President Jinping and both agreed on $280 million in tariff relief for Canadian exports, while Canada extended exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminum for two years.

Trade negotiations with the United States remain Canada's priority, though tensions persist after Washington imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion in Canadian goods, prompting retaliation from Ottawa.
Later on Nov 18, Carney will meet with Trump in Shenzhen to discuss bilateral trade, aiming to secure a deal "that is in the interest of Canadians.
title: Carney says Canada’s growing trade ties with China are not a top concern for Trump
